objectClass.notes: The screenshot is a defect reference rather than an ideal rock photo. It clearly proves the current six-to-eight-sided topology and flat face bands are unacceptable. Hidden sides may be inferred procedurally because the scatter is static and non-hero.

reasoning: The dominant close rock occupies hundreds of pixels, so its radial polygon sides and per-face shading are immediately legible.
The system repeats roughly 1600 rubble stones and 1500 pebbles, so topology must scale by projected importance rather than giving every instance hero density.
The desired surface is a continuous worn mass with a few intentional shoulder and crown breaks, not a uniformly faceted assembled solid.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate depth is required because the individual object is simple but close-range silhouette quality, repeated multi-resolution variants, slope seating, and material breakup all affect the result.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Exact mineral composition and hidden-side fractures are not recoverable from the screenshot; use a plausible northern New Mexico sandstone/volcanic palette and deterministic procedural erosion.
The screenshot does not provide neutral look-dev lighting, so judge this pass primarily on silhouette continuity and shading continuity.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: The dominant rock must have a continuously curved, asymmetrical outline without six-to-eight readable radial sides.
A broad worn shoulder should transition gradually into the upper crown instead of forming one horizontal polygon band.
The crown needs a few localized chips and an off-center high point, not a pyramidal tip.
The base must remain partially buried with a narrow cavity-darkened dust band rather than a floating black wedge.
Subtle warm/cool color variation must break up large surfaces without recreating per-triangle color blocks.
Nearby pebbles need rounded compressed silhouettes with enough segments to avoid pentagonal outlines.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At the screenshot viewpoint, no near-field rock exposes a readable radial polygon count or broad flat-shaded face bands.
Large stones select high-detail continuous-sculpt variants; medium rubble and pebbles retain cheaper variants within eight fixed InstancedMesh shape draws.
Stone silhouettes remain asymmetric and weathered, with worn shoulders, off-center crowns, localized chips, and embedded ground contact.
The merged scene retains the existing scatter counts, deterministic placement, slope alignment, collision exclusions, and production frame-rate target.

featureGroups.name: Continuous near-field stone silhouette
qualityCriteria: Near-field rock outlines use enough angular samples that individual radial sides are not readable at the screenshot scale.
The profile remains irregular and eroded rather than becoming a perfect ellipsoid.
failureModes: large rock reads as a cone, pyramid, or stretched primitive

featureGroups.name: Eroded shoulder and crown structure
qualityCriteria: Vertical profile contains enough smoothly varying rings to form a worn lower body, shoulder, crown, and embedded base.
Localized crown chips do not create a global low-poly appearance.
failureModes: one horizontal shoulder band dominates the body
top converges to a pyramidal point

featureGroups.name: Detail-scaled batching
qualityCriteria: Large rubble selects higher radial/ring density variants while ordinary rubble and pebbles use medium-density continuous variants.
Rubble and gravel remain eight fixed InstancedMesh variant draws instead of thousands of WebGPU BatchedMesh sub-draws.
failureModes: every tiny stone pays the hero topology cost
variant quality is random rather than correlated with physical size
draw calls increase with silhouette quality

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.

authoringInstruction: Fill observed object class, complexity reasoning, featureGroups, visualDeltaChecks, and unknowns before generating or implementing ObjectSculptSpec.
